statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low; Stress is extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains EA_ON; Tail is below the blocking threshold while the 12:30 UTC data and multi-stage FOMC sequence remain conditional checkpoints.
headline: Low Tail, extreme Stress ahead of U.S. data and FOMC
body: Fresh Asian-session reporting shows the 10-year Treasury yield back below 5% and oil easing but still above $100. Fresh supplementary breadth remains conflicted, with broad megacap weakness but firmer semiconductors. Current evidence does not independently verify persistent one-way NQ structure.

lookbackSummary: Across the previous 24 UTC clock-hours, Tail ranged from 17% to 23%, moving between EA_ON and WATCH; Stress ranged from 92% to 99% and dominant mode remained mixed.
outlookSummary: Tail remains low overnight and rises to WATCH around the 12:30 UTC data, the U.S. cash open and the multi-stage FOMC sequence, peaking at 24%. Escalation beyond WATCH requires observed persistent one-way structure or failed retracements.

forecast.analysis: Fresh Reuters reporting shows Asian equities cautiously firmer while the U.S. 10-year yield eased to 4.9875% and Brent fell to $107.82. Fresh Finviz context is conflicted: six of eight megacaps are lower while five of seven semiconductors are higher. Persistent one-way NQ structure is not independently verified.

forecast.analysis: Overnight liquidity remains thin. Tail stays low unless NQ begins holding an extreme while retracements repeatedly fail; elevated rates, energy prices and geopolitical risk keep Stress extreme.
drivers: Failed retracements are the key escalation test

forecast.analysis: Low Tail assumes overnight discovery remains two-sided. A sustained break with shallow pullbacks plus renewed yield or oil pressure would be the main conditional escalation path.
drivers: Shallow pullbacks would be a warning
Rates and oil remain conditional amplifiers

forecast.analysis: Approaching the European handoff, the key checkpoint is whether any overnight move survives ordinary retracement attempts. Without that persistence, the structure remains mixed.
drivers: Overnight extreme-holding is the persistence test

forecast.analysis: European participation should deepen liquidity. Tail remains low unless NQ holds an overnight extreme and cross-asset pressure aligns rather than rotates.
Early Europe is a persistence test: ordinary pullbacks would argue against Tail escalation, while repeated rejection of retracements would move risk higher.
Cross-asset confirmation becomes more informative as Europe develops. Conflicted megacap and semiconductor breadth keeps Tail below WATCH unless current NQ structure turns one-way.
drivers: Megacap weakness conflicts with firmer semiconductors

forecast.analysis: U.S. premarket participation should rise. The 12:30 UTC data remain ahead, so event importance raises Stress more than Tail before an outcome or post-release path is observed.
drivers: Event risk raises Stress before Tail

forecast.analysis: Pre-data positioning can become fragile. WATCH reflects proximity to the 12:30 UTC releases; Tail would require directional persistence after the data rather than expectations alone.
drivers: Post-release persistence is the Tail test

forecast.analysis: Retail Sales and import/export prices are scheduled for 12:30 UTC. Upper WATCH reflects the checkpoint itself; any further escalation depends on the actual post-release path and cross-asset confirmation.
drivers: Post-release persistence is the Tail test

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash open occurs at 13:30 UTC after the data. Upper WATCH is conditional on opening-auction continuation, extreme-holding or repeated failed pullbacks; ordinary retracement would reduce Tail.
During the first full post-open hour, Tail should recede if price discovery becomes two-sided. Persistent extension after failed retracements would keep the risk window active.
Late-morning U.S. trade is less event-dense. Tail remains WATCH only if earlier directional structure persists; otherwise mixed rotation would favor normalization.
FOMC positioning becomes more important as the decision approaches. Tail is WATCH because the sequence can produce multi-stage repricing, but the future direction remains unknown.
The pre-FOMC staging hour reaches upper WATCH. The 18:00 UTC decision is still unobserved; only actual persistent price-path alignment would justify a higher Tail band.
The FOMC decision is scheduled at 18:00 UTC and the press conference at 18:30 UTC. Upper WATCH reflects multi-stage repricing risk, not a presumed policy outcome or market reaction.
The press-conference and Q&A phase can generate a second information wave. Upper WATCH persists conditionally if price, yields and index leadership align without meaningful retracement.
drivers: Retracement quality after the initial move

forecast.analysis: The post-Q&A power-hour window remains upper WATCH because delayed repricing can extend. Tail would fall quickly if retracements reappear and cross-assets stabilize.
The cash-close and immediate post-FOMC transition remain a conditional delayed-second-leg window. WATCH persists only if one-way structure survives into the close.
After the U.S. close, Tail should ease if the FOMC move has become two-sided and cross-asset volatility is settling. Stress remains high from rates, oil and unresolved policy repricing.
Later after-hours trade is less liquid. Tail returns below WATCH unless a persistent post-FOMC move continues without meaningful retracement.
Overnight conditions after the U.S. session favor low Tail if cross-assets stabilize. Any renewed geopolitical or rates shock would raise Stress first unless NQ persistence also appears.
Into the next Asian session, low Tail assumes no unresolved one-way second leg from the FOMC sequence. Confidence gradually falls as the forecast horizon extends.
In the final forecast hour, low Tail assumes post-FOMC markets have restored meaningful retracement. A still-unresolved one-way second leg would invalidate that normalization case.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour: fresh rates, oil and supplementary breadth evidence is conflicted, and direct persistent NQ mean-reversion failure is not verified; Tail remains low.
Thin overnight liquidity can amplify moves, but Tail stays low unless NQ holds an extreme and retracements repeatedly fail.
Low Tail assumes two-sided overnight discovery; shallow pullbacks with renewed yield or oil pressure would be the escalation test.
The European handoff is the next persistence checkpoint; ordinary retracement would keep the structure mixed.
Deeper European liquidity should clarify whether any overnight move can hold an extreme with cross-asset confirmation.
Early Europe remains low Tail unless repeated retracement attempts fail and directional persistence strengthens.
